newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates high, trade slow.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates high, trade slow.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were steady to higher in slow morning trade on Monday although demand was not entirely met, dealers said.
Fresh trade was put at a meagre 12.8 million kuna, but lenders were said to be reluctant to meet extra demand by some borrowers.
"There is more demand and still some funds in supply, but borrowers and lenders cannot agree on terms," one dealer said.
Roughly two thirds of the morning's total were call money loans, granted at an unchanged 11 percent rate.
Seven-day interbank rate was flat at 12 percent, but the price of two-week funds rose to 14 percent from last week's 13.
One savings bank paid 16 percent for one-month funds.
The weekend trade totalled 16.2 million kuna with eight banks seeking funds to cover their shortfalls. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
